title: Every coin type explained
h1: Every type of coin, how people trade it, and what can go wrong
seo_title: Every crypto coin type explained: examples, strategies, risks and red flags
description: Bitcoin, layer 1s, layer 2s, stablecoins, staking tokens, DeFi, oracles, memecoins, AI, DePIN, RWA, gaming, perps, prediction markets, privacy coins and new launches: what each is, examples, strategies, risks, red flags.
summary: Seventeen kinds of coins across all chains: what each one is, one or two real examples, how people trade or hold it, the main risks and the red flags.
plain: Coins are not all the same. Bitcoin, a stablecoin and a two-hour-old memecoin behave completely differently, and a strategy that works on one can wipe you out on another.
Each section below says what the type is in plain words, gives real examples (examples, not picks), and lists how people trade it and what goes wrong.
dont_lose: Match your position size to the type. Memecoins and new launches get the smallest size; bitcoin and stablecoins can be bigger.
Always check the contract address, not the ticker. Copycat tokens use the same names.
Keep long-term holdings in self-custody on a hardware wallet, and only trade from a hot wallet.
Don't buy anything because it promises a fixed high return. That is the signature of a scam.
Read the unlock schedule before buying a new token.
risk: Not financial advice; no strategy wins every trade. Coins named here are examples of a category, not recommendations. Prices and yields are dated and change constantly.

items.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
items.summary: The first cryptocurrency and the largest by market value. New supply is released on a fixed schedule that halves roughly every four years. Many people treat it as a long-term store of value, and big funds hold it through spot ETFs.
glance: High for an asset, low for crypto
Macro news, rates, ETF flows, stock market risk mood
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Dollar-cost averaging (DCA): buying a fixed amount on a schedule so you never have to time the market.
Hold long term in self-custody, ideally on a hardware wallet.
Swing trading ranges and key levels, with a stop below the level.
Rebalancing: trimming after big rallies and adding after big drops, back to a target % of your portfolio.
Main risks
Drawdowns of 30% or more happen regularly. On Oct 25, 2026 it was about 36% below its all-time high, even in what many call a bull market.
Leverage gets liquidated on sudden wicks.
Exchange custody risk if you leave it on an exchange.
Rate decisions and stock market sell-offs move it.
Red flags
"Bitcoin doubler" or guaranteed-return schemes.
Wrapped or "bridged" BTC on unknown chains.
Fake BTC giveaways from impersonated celebrities.

facts.text: Bitcoin closed the week of Oct 19-25, 2026 at about $80,154, its third losing week in a row and about 36% below its Oct 6, 2025 all-time high of $126,080. Spot bitcoin ETFs held about $104.7B.

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

facts.text: About 76,805 blocks were left until the April 2028 halving as of Oct 26, 2026.

items.name: Ethereum and other layer 1s (ETH, SOL, BNB)
items.summary: Layer 1s are base blockchains that run apps, tokens and DeFi. Their coins pay transaction fees and can usually be staked to help secure the network. Ethereum is the largest. Solana is known for speed and memecoin trading. BNB powers BNB Chain.
glance: BTC, network activity, upgrades, ETF flows
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Hold and stake for yield, directly or through a liquid staking token.
Trade the ETH/BTC or SOL/ETH ratio when you have a view on relative strength.
Position ahead of major upgrades, and take profit into the news, since upgrades are often 'sell the news' events.
Swing trade trend pullbacks with stops.
Main risks
They usually fall harder than BTC when the market turns risk-off.
Competition between chains.
Network outages or failed upgrades.
Concentration among validators.
Red flags
"New Ethereum" clones with no users.
Unofficial staking sites promising fixed high returns.

facts.text: Ethereum staking hit a record 43.8M ETH, about 35.9% of supply, per Bitwise.

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

facts.text: Solana switched on its Alpenglow consensus upgrade on Oct 21, 2026. It targets about 150 ms finality (the point where a transaction can no longer be reversed), down from about six seconds.

items.name: Layer 2s (ARB, OP)
items.summary: Layer 2s are networks built on top of Ethereum. They batch transactions so they are cheaper and faster, then settle back to Ethereum. Their tokens are mostly used for governance. Some big L2s, such as Base, have no token of their own.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Trade around ecosystem incentive programmes and big app launches.
Watch token-unlock calendars, since big unlocks often bring selling pressure.
Hold as a small part of an ETH-ecosystem basket.
Main risks
How the token captures value is often unclear.
Large insider and treasury supply unlocking over time.
Centralised sequencers (the single operator that orders transactions) and upgrade keys.
Red flags
"L2 airdrop claim" links in replies.
Brand-new L2 tokens with most of the supply locked and a tiny float.

items.name: Stablecoins (USDC, USDT)
items.summary: Tokens built to stay at $1, usually backed by cash and short-term government bonds held by an issuer. People use them for trading, payments, and parking value between trades.
glance: Very low while the peg holds
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Keep your 'dry powder' (cash ready for trades) in stablecoins between trades.
Earn lending or savings yield (see How to earn).
Spread holdings across issuers rather than trusting one.
Main risks
Depeg (losing the $1 price) under stress.
Issuers can freeze tokens at specific addresses.
Algorithmic designs have collapsed before, for example Terra's UST in May 2022.
Rules differ by country.
Red flags
"Stablecoins" paying 20%+ with no clear source of the yield.
Unknown stablecoins with a tiny pool.

facts.text: Total stablecoin supply was about $304.2B on Oct 25, 2026 (DefiLlama data, cited by CoinLab). The US OCC became the first regulator to finalise rules under the GENIUS Act on stablecoins.

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

items.name: Liquid staking and restaking tokens (stETH, JitoSOL, weETH)
items.summary: You stake a coin through a protocol and get a token back that earns the staking reward while staying tradable. Restaking tokens (LRTs) put that stake to work securing extra services for extra reward, which adds extra risk.
glance: The underlying coin; occasional discount to it
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Hold instead of the plain coin to earn staking yield.
Buy at a discount to the underlying coin when markets panic, if you understand why the discount is there.
Use as collateral in lending, carefully, because looping (borrowing against it to buy more) raises your liquidation risk.
Main risks
Smart contract bugs.
Slashing (validators losing part of their stake as a penalty).
Trading at a discount when everyone wants out at once.
Restaking adds layers of risk for small extra yield.
Red flags
Yields far above the market rate for staking that coin.
Unaudited LST forks.

facts.text: Yields on Oct 27, 2026: Lido stETH about 2.24%, JitoSOL about 4.75%, ether.fi weETH about 2.31% (DefiLlama). These change daily.

items.name: DeFi tokens (AAVE, UNI, JUP)
items.summary: Tokens of lending markets, exchanges and aggregators. Some share fees with holders or buy back tokens. Many only give voting rights.
glance: Usage, fees, buybacks, unlocks, market mood
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Compare fees and revenue with market value (price-to-fees), the same way you would value a business.
Buy leaders on pullbacks when usage is growing.
Avoid holding through big unlocks.
Main risks
Hacks and exploits.
Regulation.
Tokens with no claim on fees.
They fall hardest when the market turns risk-off.
Red flags
Big TVL that is mostly paid-for incentives.
Anonymous team, no audit, upgradeable contracts with one key.

facts.text: In the week of Oct 19-25, 2026, AAVE fell about 10.3% and MORPHO about 16.9% while bitcoin fell 2.4%. DeFi led the dip. Aerodrome and Velodrome merged into one DEX called Aero.

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

items.name: Infrastructure and oracle tokens (LINK, PYTH)
items.summary: Oracles bring outside data, such as prices, on-chain so apps can use it. Other infrastructure tokens pay for storage, data indexing or cross-chain messaging.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Hold as a long-term bet that blockchains get used more.
Trade around big integration news, often selling into the headline.
Main risks
Partnership news that never turns into revenue.
Large token supply still to unlock.
Red flags
"Partnership" claims you cannot find on the partner's own site.

items.name: Established memecoins (DOGE, BONK, WIF, PEPE)
items.summary: Memecoins that have survived long enough to build deep liquidity and a lasting community. They move on attention and market mood.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Trend and level trading with stops; no leverage.
Rotation: attention moves between memecoins in waves.
Take profit into hype spikes.
Main risks
Drawdowns of 70-90% are common.
The whole category can go out of fashion.
Red flags
Copycat tickers on other chains.
Paid influencer waves.

facts.text: Memecoins stayed green in the week of Oct 19-25, 2026 (PEPE about +9.1%) while DeFi tokens fell. Attention-driven coins can decouple from the rest of the market, in both directions.

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

items.name: New memecoin launches (pump.fun and fresh pairs)
items.summary: Brand-new tokens launched in minutes, often on a bonding curve (a pricing formula where the price rises automatically as people buy) before they 'graduate' to a DEX pool.
examples: Fresh pump.fun launches (no specific coin named on purpose)
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Follow the full playbook: safety checks, survival hold, a small fixed size, partial profits at 2x, and a time stop.
Main risks
Most launches go to zero.
Rugs and honeypots.
Bundled insider supply.
Fees of several % per round trip.
Red flags
Anything pushed hard in its first hour.
Big holder clusters.
Authorities still on.

facts.text: Solidus Labs reported that 98.6% of pump.fun tokens created between January 2024 and March 2025 fell below $1,000 of liquidity (pump.fun disputed the framing).

src.label: Solidus Labs, Solana rug pulls and pump-and-dumps report

items.name: AI and AI-agent tokens (VIRTUAL, TAO)
items.summary: Tokens linked to AI: networks that reward machine-learning work, such as Bittensor's TAO, and launchpads for on-chain AI agents, such as Virtuals.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Trade the narrative in waves, taking profit into AI headlines.
Separate real usage from 'AI' labels on token pages.
Main risks
Many 'AI' tokens have no product.
AI stock sell-offs spill over into these tokens.
Red flags
"AI trading bot" tokens that promise returns.
Agent tokens where the dev holds a large share of supply.

items.name: DePIN (HNT, RENDER)
items.summary: DePIN stands for decentralised physical infrastructure networks. They pay tokens to people who provide real-world resources such as wireless coverage, GPU compute or storage.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Compare revenue from real customers with token emissions (newly created tokens paid out).
Hold as a long-term bet if usage is growing.
Main risks
Emissions can be far bigger than real demand.
Hardware costs if you take part as a provider.
Red flags
"Buy this miner to earn passive income" sales pitches.

items.name: Real-world assets, RWA (ONDO, BUIDL)
items.summary: Real-world assets are tokens that represent things like government bonds, money-market funds or stocks on-chain. Some are only open to qualified or institutional investors.
glance: Low for the asset tokens, high for governance tokens
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Hold tokenised bond funds for yield, where you are allowed to.
Trade RWA governance tokens on adoption news.
Main risks
Legal and issuer risk.
Redemption limits.
Fakes using real brand names.
Red flags
"Tokenised stock airdrops" and claim pages.
RWA tokens you cannot redeem anywhere.

facts.text: JPMorgan brought tokenised money-market funds to Solana, and the SEC added tokenisation to its fiscal 2027 exam priorities (both reported in the week of Oct 19-25, 2026).

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

items.name: Gaming and NFT tokens (IMX, AXS)
items.summary: Tokens of gaming networks, games and NFT ecosystems. They are used for in-game items, fees and rewards.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Trade around big game launches.
Check real player numbers, not just trailers.
Main risks
Play-to-earn economies that collapse when new players stop coming.
Bridge hacks.
Red flags
Fake game 'beta' downloads (often malware).
NFT mint links in DMs.

items.name: Perpetuals and derivatives tokens (HYPE, DYDX)
items.summary: Tokens of perpetual-futures exchanges. Perpetuals (perps) are futures with no expiry date, often traded with leverage. Some of these tokens get value from buybacks paid for by fees.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Compare fees and buybacks with market value.
Farm points on new venues only with money you would trade anyway (see How to earn).
Main risks
Leverage liquidations: in one day in October 2026, more than $800M of positions were force-closed.
Exchange or oracle exploits.
Points programmes that never become a token.
Red flags
Venues with self-reported volume and no audit.
Points 'guaranteed to convert'.

facts.text: On Oct 24, 2026 more than $810M was liquidated across the market in 24 hours, about $689M of it long positions (Bitcoin.com News via CoinLab).

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

facts.text: In 2026 some perp DEX points programmes paid out (for example Lighter gave 25% of LIT to points holders on Dec 30, 2025), while others ended with no token (StandX cancelled its token on Oct 15, 2026).

src.label: dexwatch, perp DEX points programmes in Q4 2026

items.name: Prediction markets (Polymarket, Kalshi)
items.summary: Markets where you buy 'yes' or 'no' shares on real-world events. Each share pays $1 if it is right and $0 if it is wrong. You trade outcome shares, not a coin.
glance: Event-driven; goes to $0 or $1 at the end
Deep on big markets, thin on small ones
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Only bet where you have a real information edge.
Treat the price as a probability: buying 'yes' at $0.30 means you think the chance is above 30%.
Size small, because every share can go to zero.
Main risks
Rules about how a market resolves can be ambiguous.
Legal limits in some countries.
Thin markets are easy to move.
Red flags
"Insider tips" groups selling picks.
Copycat prediction-market sites.

facts.text: October 2026 was reported as a record month for prediction markets, with Kalshi passing Polymarket in monthly volume for the first time. The two venues count volume differently, so compare with care.

src.label: Predictable, Kalshi overtakes Polymarket as October trading surges
pdata, how prediction-market venues count volume

items.name: Privacy coins (ZEC, XMR)
items.summary: Coins that can hide who sent how much to whom. Zcash makes privacy optional. Monero makes it the default.
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Trade the narrative around upgrades.
Hold small if you value privacy.
Main risks
Exchange delistings in some countries.
Narrative-driven rallies can reverse hard.
Red flags
"Untraceable" mixers promising to clean funds (often scams or illegal).

facts.text: Zcash was the best top-10 performer in the week of Oct 19-25, 2026 (about +7.3%) ahead of its NU7 upgrade, planned for early November.

src.label: CoinLab, crypto market weekly review Oct 19-25, 2026

items.name: New launches, presales and airdrops
items.summary: A TGE (token generation event) is when a new token first goes live. Presales sell tokens before launch. Airdrops and points reward early users with tokens.
examples: Upcoming TGEs listed by trackers (no picks)
lists: Ways people trade or hold it
Farm airdrops with small, real usage you would do anyway.
Wait for the post-launch selling to settle before buying.
Read the token unlock schedule before buying.
Main risks
Most presales underperform or fail.
Airdrops can be smaller than you expect, or cancelled.
Fake claim sites appear the day a token launches.
Red flags
Presales sold through DMs or Telegram only.
"Guaranteed listing" or guaranteed-multiple claims.
No public team, no audit, no published token supply split.

items: Pick the type, then use the risk rules and sizing from the memecoin playbook, scaled to how volatile that type is.
For Solana-specific detail, read the Solana guide.
Look up any unfamiliar word in the glossary.
